title: The Art of Love
author: Ovid
translator: Henry T. Riley, 1885 (public domain, Project Gutenberg #47677)
blurb: Rome's cheekiest poet writes a mock-serious handbook on romance — so popular, and so naughty, that the emperor exiled him.

compliments.e: He paid her compliments on her cooking.

fair.m: (Old use) a beautiful woman; the beloved.
fair.e: Poets wrote endless songs to the fair.

cards.title: Love as a campaign
cards.text: Ovid jokes that a lover is like a new soldier: first find someone to love, then win them by pleasing, then make the love last.
cards.quote: are now coming for the first time to engage as a soldier in a new service.
cards.qMean: Starting a romance is like signing up for a new campaign.
cards.qLife: Planning a first date like a careful project.
cards.cap: Mongez, Mars and Venus · public domain

cards.title: Please first
cards.text: The second task, he says, is simply to please — kindness and attention come before any grand gesture.
cards.quote: The next task after that, is to prevail on the fair by pleasing her.
cards.qMean: The next step is to win them over by being pleasant.
cards.qLife: Remembering someone's favourite tea before trying to impress them.
cards.cap: Vénus et Adonis (Nicolas Poussin) · public domain

cards.title: Write it down
cards.text: Ovid advises sending letters full of compliments — words reach where you cannot.
cards.qMean: Let your message carry your praise.
cards.qLife: A thoughtful text after a first meeting.
cards.cap: 'Sappho' with writing tablets, Pompeii fresco · public domain

cards.title: Don't overdo it
cards.text: He tells men not to fuss too much over looks; heroes of myth won hearts without curling their hair.
cards.quote: A neglect of beauty becomes men
cards.qMean: Men don't need to over-groom to be attractive.
cards.qLife: Clean and simple beats ten hair products.
cards.cap: Hercules and Omphale by F.Goya · public domain

cards.title: The danger of easy promises
cards.text: Ovid cheekily says lovers promise everything — and the gods laugh at lovers' broken vows. Read it as satire: two thousand years ago, people already knew sweet talk is cheap.
cards.qMean: Promises are attractive — which is why they're easily made.
cards.qLife: Be wary of someone who promises the moon on day one.
cards.cap: Francesco Bartolozzi - Nymph and Cupid · public domain
